input_text: Today we are discussing hyper tension and hypotension. Hyper tension means high blood pressure and hypotension means low blood pressure. These terms describe different conditions and should remain clearly distinct. The first patient has resistance, hyper tension and chronic kidney disease. The second patient has orthostatic hypotension, there is no evidence of primary outlawed in either patient. The report includes systolic blood pressure, the astolic blood pressure, high rate and kidney function. Blood pressure increase by 10 mm of mercury. The recorded dose was 5 mg, not 15 mg. We also reviewed physical activity and physical inactivity. The patient discussed cardiovascular risks, lifestyle modifications and pharmacological therapy. Several blood pressure measurements were recorded by the clinical team. Finally, the report states that there is no edema, no chest pain and no shortness of breath. This negative findings, most remain unchanged in the translation
